callout.text: A grave, not a bill of sale

storyboard.claim: Sethe chose a grave for her daughter over a bill of sale for herself.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A grave icon: the burial place she chose, read literally.
storyboard.onScreenText: A grave, not a bill of sale
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Cold open: the book's central choice.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the two options so the grave reads as a deliberate trade, not an accident.

storyboard.claim: The tension between love and calculation is the core of this analysis.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sethe thinking over a sum: the calculation itself is the subject, no icon needed.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows the question of love or arithmetic.
storyboard.addedInformation: Gives the abstract word 'calculation' a face doing the sum.

storyboard.claim: The popular reading of the novel as a ghost story is rejected.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The rejected label, struck through. A ghost icon would be unreadable, so none is drawn.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the common reading the hosts are about to reject.
storyboard.addedInformation: The strike shows the reading is being crossed out, not endorsed.

storyboard.claim: The true haunting is the ledger that records people as property.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The schoolteacher holding a ledger of notes: the record of people as property.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the ghost reading to the ledger reading.
storyboard.addedInformation: Puts the ledger in the schoolteacher's hand so it reads as a record kept by a person.

storyboard.claim: Enslavement made people literal property on a balance sheet.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The schoolteacher with the notebook, the instrument of the count.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains what the ledger does to people.
storyboard.addedInformation: Says plainly that people were entered as property; no balance icon, which would read as fairness.

storyboard.claim: The reader must do the impossible accounting that the characters were forced to do.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sethe thinking over an impossible sum, the accounting of the book.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the ledger itself to the reader's task.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes the 'reader does the math' idea a character thinking through a sum.

storyboard.claim: The novel's terror lives in the house at 124 Bluestone Road, not in a ghost.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A home icon for the house, with Sethe pointing toward it.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns from the reader's task to the place where the book's terror is.
storyboard.addedInformation: Gives the address as the title of the house, anchoring the place name.

storyboard.claim: The story is set in the dead of winter in Ohio, on the road to the house.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A dirt road in a cold setting, Sethe walking toward the house.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Sets the physical place after pointing at the house.
storyboard.addedInformation: Puts the viewer on the road, not in a ghost house.

storyboard.claim: Sethe escaped a Kentucky plantation to reach Ohio.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A road icon for the escape route north, Sethe thinking back on it.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces Sethe's past after the setting.
storyboard.addedInformation: Road icon shows the escape journey literally.

storyboard.claim: The plantation name Sweet Home is an irony, and three people are introduced: Sethe, Denver and Paul D.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sethe, Denver and Paul D together, the three people the story turns on.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From Sethe's escape to the people who live with her and the men from the past.
storyboard.addedInformation: Three distinct figures stand for the three characters introduced in one sentence.

storyboard.claim: Paul D arrives at the porch eighteen years after they last saw each other.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A door icon for the house threshold, Paul D walking up to it.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Brings the returning man to the house.
storyboard.addedInformation: Door icon marks the threshold he crosses.

storyboard.claim: The tension between Sethe and Paul D is thick.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sethe and Paul D facing each other, both thinking, two different builds.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the arrival to the tension of the meeting.
storyboard.addedInformation: Two distinct figures show the two people in tension.

callout.text: They are legally free, still cataloged

storyboard.claim: They are legally free but psychologically still cataloged as property.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Paul D thinking, sad, the weight of the record on him.
storyboard.onScreenText: They are legally free, still cataloged
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains why the arrival is tense.
storyboard.addedInformation: Separates legal freedom from the mental record of enslavement.

storyboard.claim: The enslaved were priced and itemized alongside cattle and equipment.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The schoolteacher with his notebook, the one who itemized them.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows how the record was kept.
storyboard.addedInformation: Ties the itemizing to the notebook in the hand of the person who did it.

storyboard.claim: Psychological captivity does not end just because a document was signed.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Chains icon for captivity that continues, Sethe slumped under it.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains why freedom on paper is not enough.
storyboard.addedInformation: Chains read as bound and imprisoned, the literal meaning here.

storyboard.claim: The analysis asks how people calculate the cost of freedom against the cost of love.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sethe thinking about the two costs, worried.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: States the central question of the analysis.
storyboard.addedInformation: Frames the question as a choice made by a person.

storyboard.claim: The ledger is structurally impossible to balance.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sethe thinking, sad, over an impossible sum.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Returns to the ledger metaphor as the frame for the house.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the impossibility in plain words.

callout.text: The house is an account book

storyboard.claim: 124 Bluestone Road is the physical account book where the debts are recorded.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Home icon for the house, Sethe pointing at it as the record.
storyboard.onScreenText: The house is an account book
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the ledger idea to the house itself.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes the house the record of the debts.

callout.text: An active participant in the math

storyboard.claim: The house is not just a container but an active part of the calculation.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sethe in the kitchen, thinking, the house as an active presence around her.
storyboard.onScreenText: An active participant in the math
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows the house as account book with its role in the sum.
storyboard.addedInformation: The kitchen set shows the house as the place where the math happens.

storyboard.claim: The sensory reality of the house is freezing cold.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sethe in a cold kitchen, thinking, breath in the cold.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the framework to the sensory details of the house.
storyboard.addedInformation: Puts the cold on the set and on the woman in it.

storyboard.claim: Handprints appear in a cake and a kettle of chickpeas smokes: the house's spirit activity.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sethe pointing at the cake in the kitchen, afraid. No child figure is drawn.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Starts the list of the house's sensory events.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the event through the mother's fear, no child figure.

storyboard.claim: A mirror shatters in the house, another relentless event.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sethe afraid in the kitchen, the mirror is named in the callout.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the list of events in the house.
storyboard.addedInformation: The callout names the shattering event; no mirror icon, which would read as self-image.

storyboard.claim: The boys stuff quilt packing into their hats to muffle the sound of the house.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sethe thinking, worried, about the muffled sound.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows how the household copes with the house.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the muffling action in the callout.

storyboard.claim: The boys creep away from a house that is throwing what Denver calls a powerful spell.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Denver walking away from the house door, afraid.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the reaction to the house's activity.
storyboard.addedInformation: Door icon marks the house they leave.

storyboard.claim: The house acts like a spiteful, venomous tantrum, not a Gothic castle.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sethe thinking, worried. The tantrum is named in the callout, no child figure.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Characterizes the house's behavior after the escape.
storyboard.addedInformation: Frames the house as spiteful rather than spooky.

callout.text: A tally of what is owed

storyboard.claim: The house is not a castle; it keeps a tally of what is owed.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The schoolteacher's notebook, the tally of debts.
storyboard.onScreenText: A tally of what is owed
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Connects the house to the ledger again.
storyboard.addedInformation: Ties the tally to the record-keeping figure.

storyboard.claim: The house is named only by a number, not by a grand plantation name.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sethe pointing at the house number.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains the address as the name of the house.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the plain number as the house identity.

storyboard.claim: The house is a piece of property with no romance in its name.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The schoolteacher holding the record of property.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the number as property.
storyboard.addedInformation: Puts the property in the record-keeper's hand.

storyboard.claim: The house claims property rights over the people trapped inside it.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sethe afraid, thinking, under the claim of the house.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves the property idea to the people inside.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the people as the thing being claimed.

storyboard.claim: Sethe's transaction with the engraver is one of the most devastating in American literature.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sethe thinking, sad, about the transaction at the cemetery.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces the engraver transaction.
storyboard.addedInformation: Frames the deal as a transaction, not a romance.

storyboard.claim: Sethe needs to put a name on her baby girl's headstone.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sethe thinking, sad, about the stone. No child figure is drawn.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Sets up the cost of the headstone.
storyboard.addedInformation: Says what she needs without staging the child.

storyboard.claim: Sethe has no money and operates outside the economy; she has nothing to pay with.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sethe slumped, sad, with nothing in her hands.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains why she had to trade for the stone.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the lack of money through the empty hands.

storyboard.claim: The payment bought seven letters for the word BELOVED.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sethe thinking, sad, about the seven letters on the stone.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names what the payment bought.
storyboard.addedInformation: Gives the count of letters so viewers can hold the number.

storyboard.claim: Sethe was coerced into degrading sexual exploitation in exchange for the letters; the harm is named plainly.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sethe thinking, sad. No intimacy staging, no bed; the harm is named in the callout.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the price of the letters.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the coerced exchange without depicting any act.

storyboard.claim: Sethe did not have the currency to buy the word dearly.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sethe thinking, sad, about the word she could not buy.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the price of the word.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the missing word in the callout.

storyboard.claim: Sethe does the arithmetic of grief with the only currency she has.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sethe thinking, sad, over the sum of grief.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Generalizes the transaction into the book's arithmetic.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the arithmetic as grief, not money.

storyboard.claim: The baby's death and the mother's dignity spent to buy the name are the foundational entry of the haunting.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A grave icon, Sethe thinking, sad. No child figure.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Closes the cemetery transaction.
storyboard.addedInformation: Frames the grave as the price paid for the name.

storyboard.claim: The house is a ledger: a massive deficit accumulates.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sethe thinking, worried, about the deficit.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the cemetery deal into the house's ledger.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the deficit plainly.

storyboard.claim: The mild reading of the house as a frustrated accountant is rejected.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The struck-through phrase carries the rejection; no accountant icon.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Rejects the milder reading of the house.
storyboard.addedInformation: The strike shows the reading is crossed out.

storyboard.claim: The text shows a house that is purely malicious; no dog injury is staged.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sethe afraid in the kitchen, thinking. The violence is carried by the callout, not drawn.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Begins the account of the house's violence.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the malice in words instead of staging harm to any creature.
